title: OpenAI pays $3.2 million to settle US worker bias claim
excerpt: OpenAI disputes the Justice Department's view, but said it wanted to move forward with a program to support employees "requiring immigration support."
content_html:
The Justice Department said OpenAI and one of its subsidiaries discriminated against US workers by unfairly favoring workers with temporary visa status during the hiring process.

On Tuesday, the Justice Department announced that OpenAI and Statsig, a subsidiary software development company based in Bellevue, Washington, would pay $3.2 million to settle the allegations.

"It is illegal to discriminate against U.S. workers by preferring temporary visa holders for jobs," Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon said in a statement. "This substantial settlement ensures that OpenAI redresses harm and changes its recruitment practices so that U.S. workers receive a fair opportunity for highly sought-after technology positions."

OpenAI said it disagreed with the DOJ's findings, but settled the matter so it could move forward with a program to support employees "requiring immigration support."

"OpenAI's mission is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement. "Fulfilling that mission and maintaining America's leadership in AI requires attracting and retaining the best talent from the United States and around the world.

"While we disagree with the DOJ's findings, we reached this agreement to resolve the matter and move forward with our PERM program, which is critical for employees and candidates requiring immigration support."

The Justice Department said it found "reasonable cause" to believe that both companies made it more difficult for US workers to apply for positions they hoped to fill with foreign workers through Permanent Labor Certification, a process known as PERM.

The Trump administration has sought to crack down on companies it has said are abusing the visa system. The PERM program allows companies to sponsor temporary visa holders for permanent status, but only if they cannot find US workers for the job following a good-faith recruitment effort.

The DOJ said OpenAI and Statsig failed to take several steps critical to the PERM process, including failing to post some jobs on external sites and not advertising the positions on the radio late at night. OpenAI also required applicants for jobs it hoped to fill via PERM recruitment to mail in paper applications, even though it usually allowed electronic applications for other positions, the DOJ said.

In total, the Justice Department said, while there were fewer than 10 positions at issue across both OpenAI and Statsig, "the resolution amount reflects the harm to US workers when they are shut out of applying for lucrative technology jobs."

Of the $3.2 million settlement, OpenAI will pay $1.2 million in civil penalties. The other $2 million is being set aside to establish a fund "to compensate victims of the companies' discriminatory practices."

content_html_zh:
司法部表示，OpenAI 及其子公司之一在招聘过程中不公平地偏向拥有临时签证身份的工人，从而歧视美国工人。

周二，司法部宣布 OpenAI 和位于华盛顿州贝尔维尤的子公司软件开发公司 Statsig 将支付 320 万美元来和解指控。

助理司法部长 Harmeet K. 迪隆在一份声明中说道。 “这项实质性和解确保 OpenAI 纠正伤害并改变其招聘做法，以便美国工人获得获得高度抢手的技术职位的公平机会。”

OpenAI 表示，它不同意司法部的调查结果，但解决了此事，以便能够推进一项支持“需要移民支持”的员工的计划。

OpenAI 发言人在一份声明中表示：“OpenAI 的使命是确保 AGI 造福全人类。” “完成这一使命并保持美国在人工智能领域的领导地位需要吸引和留住来自美国和世界各地的最优秀人才。

“虽然我们不同意司法部的调查结果，但我们达成了这项协议来解决问题并推进我们的 PERM 计划，这对于需要移民支持的员工和候选人至关重要。”

司法部表示，它找到“合理的理由”相信，这两家公司让美国工人更难通过永久劳工认证（即 PERM 程序）申请他们希望由外国工人填补的职位。

特朗普政府试图打击其声称滥用签证制度的公司。 PERM 计划允许公司赞助临时签证持有者获得永久身份，但前提是他们在真诚的招聘努力后无法找到美国工人。

美国司法部表示，OpenAI 和 Statsig 未能采取对 PERM 流程至关重要的几个步骤，包括未能在外部网站上发布一些职位，以及没有在深夜在广播中发布职位广告。 美国司法部表示，OpenAI 还要求希望通过 PERM 招聘填补职位空缺的申请人邮寄纸质申请表，尽管其他职位通常允许电子申请。

司法部表示，虽然 OpenAI 和 Statsig 的争议职位总共不到 10 个，但“解决金额反映了美国工人因无法申请利润丰厚的技术工作而受到的伤害。”

在 320 万美元的和解金中，OpenAI 将支付 120 万美元的民事罚款。 另外 200 万美元将被留出设立一个基金，“补偿公司歧视行为的受害者”。
